name: MA-09
label: Safe D

key_factors: Strong Democratic district (D+6 PVI) with a Democratic environment
Keating's incumbency and large cash advantage over MacAllister
Markets price a Democratic win at ~95%
No public polling, so uncertainty rests on fundamentals
model.rationale: Keating holds a D+6 seat in a favorable national environment, has roughly $495K on hand versus $35K for MacAllister, and prediction markets price his win at about 95%. With no contrary polling or ratings, the fundamentals point to a comfortable double-digit Democratic margin.
model.watch: Any late polling showing a single-digit race or a surge of outside spending against Keating would warrant a downgrade.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Bill Keating seeks another term in a southeastern Massachusetts district that leans Democratic by six points on recent partisan performance. He enters the general election as a well-established incumbent with about $495,000 on hand, while Republican Tyler MacAllister has raised far less and holds roughly $35,000. No public general-election polls are available, and no expert raters have flagged the race as competitive.

Prediction markets give Keating about a 95% chance of winning, consistent with the district's lean and the current political environment favoring Democrats. The forecast expects a Democratic victory by roughly nineteen points, with modest uncertainty given the absence of polling.
